thread:
alice: FYI seeing a sharp spike in client errors after the SDK 0.16 rollout. lots of HTTP/2 handshake failures in the logs, customers hitting streaming endpoints are the worst. dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/alerts/hd-9089

pagerduty-bot: INC-45712 triggered by 5xx-rate > 1% over 5m for sdk-0.16 (paging oncall)

incident-bot: paging @sre-rotation (priority: P1) — please acknowledge in #incidents

ben: acked. I'm pulling logs and traces now. quick question — is this only streaming or plain generation too?

carla: initial telemetry shows ~92% of failures are on /v1/stream and /realtime/ws connections. non-streaming text gen looks mostly fine.

ben: copying some recent error lines from the canary host (canary-04):
```
ERROR 2026-05-12T09:40:12Z h2: unexpected frame type SETTINGS after HEADERS
ERROR 2026-05-12T09:40:13Z client: handshake failed: protocol error: invalid SETTINGS
ERROR 2026-05-12T09:40:14Z runtime: stream reset: REFUSED_STREAM
```

alice: those look like an http2 layer mismatch. 0.16 changed the client HTTP/2 header encoding for vanity user-agent + new compression flag. maybe a contract break with server side h2 kernel.

derek: I'm seeing increased 502s in region-eu1 specifically. Can we confirm if the rollout was region-scoped?

carla: yes it was targeted: canary 20% eu1, 10% us-west. Canary tag: release/0.16-canary-20260512-04

ben: immediate mitigation plan: 1) kill feature-flag that enables http2_client_v2 in SDK server-side routing to cut canary to 0%. 2) if that doesn't help, cut the canary deploy. 3) communicate to CS for customers on streaming.

alice: +1. If we can flip the flag in prod quickly that's fastest. Who has console access?

ben: I do. flipping now. endpoint: https://console.redwood.ai/flags

ben: running:
```
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/api/flags/toggle" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"sdk_http2_client_v2","state":"off","scope":"canary"}'
```

ben: sent. response: {"flag":"sdk_http2_client_v2","previous":"on","current":"off","applied":true}

carla: confirmed from traffic router: canary traffic to sdk-0.16 in eu1 -> 0%.

incident-bot: severity escalated to SEV1 due to customer-impacting streaming failures. Notifying execs.

ben: checking metrics — error rate down from 2.3% to 0.35% in the last 3m for eu1. latency stable.

alice: looks like the flag flip worked. great catch. can we snapshot logs and preserve the canary host for postmortem (don't auto-scale terminate)?

ben: preserved canary-04, archived /var/log/redwood/agent.log and uploaded to s3://incidents/1759519623/canary-04.tar.gz

derek: I'm drafting an initial customer impact note. early estimate: ~8 customers on streaming connections saw transient disconnects, 2 customers reported failed ingestions. I'll open a CS ticket.

carla: next steps: schedule rollback of the SDK change (PR revert) and coordinate with release owners. We should also run a compatibility test matrix against our HTTP/2 stack before re-rolling.

ben: creating rollback PR now: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/sdk/+/revert-0.16-h2-change (PR 3421). tagging @carla for review.

alice: handoff — I'm off for a hard stop in 25m. Ben will lead the follow-ups, Carla will own the postmortem. Derek will handle customer comms.

carla: will take postmortem. please add logs, pagerduty timeline, and flag flip evidence. I'll include suggested mitigations: stricter contract tests, server-side graceful fallback for unknown SETTINGS, and gating flag with integration smoke tests.

ben: rolling back canary deploy in parallel in case flag re-flip is needed. running deploy rollback: `deploy rollback release/0.16-canary-20260512-04 --to release/0.15-stable`

incident-bot: deploy rollback started by ben (task id: deploy-7731). expected completion ~10m.

ben: rollback completed. health checks green. final check shows error rate back to baseline for all regions.

derek: customer comms sent for the two impacted accounts, offering 2 hrs of engineering support and a timeline for the postmortem.

alice: thanks everyone. sitrep at 30m: incident contained, P1 remains until postmortem published. Please add any follow-ups in this thread.

carla: noted. I'll publish the postmortem draft in ~6 hours and link here. Suggested severity: SEV2 for the final record (but keeping P1 for exec visibility until postmortem).

ben: logs + flag audit + deploy timeline committed at s3://incidents/1759519623/artifacts.json

incident-bot: incident closed from auto-escalation. Final status: mitigated (root cause suspected: http2 header encoding change in SDK 0.16 causing server-side protocol errors). Postmortem owner: carla.

alice: great work. add a TODO for SDK release checklist update (http2 contract tests) and make the feature flag a release-gated toggle next time. :thumbsup:"
